headline: Democrats picked Jeffries for Speaker. The vote was 251-11.
summary: House Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker on Wednesday, 251 to 11, behind closed doors. The full House votes on Jan. 3, when Democrats take the majority with at least 257 seats against the 218 needed. He would be the first Black lawmaker to lead the chamber. Seven of the no votes were new members from the party's left.
cover_answer: Leads the House. He'd be second in line after the VP.
table_question: If your team picked a captain 251 to 11, do the 11 matter?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: The people who make our country's laws picked a new leader today. His name is Hakeem Jeffries, and 251 of them voted for him, the way a class picks a line leader. He would be the first Black person ever to run that room. The real vote is in January, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: One room, one leader, one vote they have watched happen in class.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script hands over one room and one leader, and the line-leader vote is one they have watched happen. The number 251 is the vivid feature they will keep. Expect 'did he win?' Almost. His side picked him; the whole House votes in January, and his side has the most seats.

8-12.script: Democrats won the House in November, so they get to pick its Speaker. On Wednesday they chose Hakeem Jeffries, 251 to 11. The whole House votes on Jan. 3, and his side has at least 257 seats against the 218 needed. Like a team picking its captain: the inside vote decides.
8-12.why: Win the House, then pick its leader. A chain they can count.
8-12.why_long: At nine a child is working out rules and if they hold, so the script runs a chain: win the House in November, pick the leader in a closed room, carry the open vote in January because 257 beats 218. The captain is a vote they have sat through. Expect 'why vote again in January?' The whole House gets a say, not just the winners.

13-17.script: Does 251 to 11 mean the party agrees? Seven of the no votes were new members from the left who say voters asked for change, and Jeffries promised 'the highest common denominator'. Second: Trump has pledged to veto bills he dislikes. What can a Speaker with 257 seats actually deliver?
13-17.why: Two things at once: a landslide inside, a veto waiting outside.
13-17.why_long: A fifteen-year-old can hold two true things: 251 to 11 is a landslide, and the 11 are the newest members saying the party owes voters more change. The script gives them both, then adds the veto, so a win inside one room meets a limit outside it. Expect 'so what can he pass?' Anything Trump will sign, and a fight over the rest.

5-7.q: Is he the boss of the president?
5-7.a: No. He'd lead the people who write the laws. The president is a different job.

8-12.a: Leads the House. He'd also be second in line after the VP.

8-12.q: Why did 11 of his own side vote no?
8-12.a: Seven are brand new, from the left. They say voters want more change.

13-17.q: Why does the first Black Speaker matter?
13-17.a: No Black lawmaker has ever led the House. The Caucus credits Black turnout.

13-17.q: Can he pass anything if Trump vetoes it?
13-17.a: Only with his signature or a veto override. Expect fights over costs.
